why: `aria-describedby=""` looks like absence and is not: it is still a described-by relationship, one that resolves to no element, which assistive technology reports as a broken reference rather than as a control needing no explanation. The distinction is invisible to any assertion that asks whether the reason is GONE by reading the attribute's value, which is why the cases here ask `hasAttribute` instead. Killed in ui.test.ts and in the versus-preview sweep, where the standalone Controllers panel's interactive buttons must carry no reference at all. Issue #260 raised this from 3 to 5: the versus pane's Start button now carries its refusal through the same helper, so two more assertions -- the pane's own aria-describedby checks -- fail when it is broken.
killedBy: describeDisabledReason: the reason is associated, not merely nearby REMOVES the reference rather than emptying it, so nothing points at nothing
describeDisabledReason: the reason is associated, not merely nearby never leaves a stale reason on a control that has since been enabled
hud: versus setup pane (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-21-versus-setup-menu-design.md) keyboard-only first launch is playable by default: no refusal, and exactly one human
hud: versus setup pane (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-21-versus-setup-menu-design.md) refuses Start with an actionable, ASSOCIATED reason -- and only the first offending card carries one
the UI kit contracts, swept across every control that uses them (issue #321) associates a refused Start with the reason, and describes the Controllers panel's real rows with nothing
